plain.li: I had my {ITEM} with me the whole fight and came through it. It's lucky. I'm keeping it close.
The shot that should have had me went wide. I had my {ITEM} on me. That's not a coincidence.

blunt.li: The {ITEM} is lucky. Don't touch it.

cold.li: It means nothing, statistically. I'm taking the {ITEM} into every fight regardless.

warm.li: I touch my {ITEM} before every fight now and think of the people I'm fighting for. It hasn't failed me yet.

cheerful.li: My {ITEM} is lucky! I came through that fight with it, and I'm not going into the next one without it.

gloomy.li: I had my {ITEM} and I lived. I don't know what to make of that, so I keep it near.

plain.li: I used to think my {ITEM} was lucky. I've stopped needing it, I think.

warm.li: Maybe it was never the {ITEM}. Maybe it was the people standing next to me.

cheerful.li: My {ITEM} can just be my {ITEM} again. Maybe I'm the lucky one!

gloomy.li: Luck never lived in my {ITEM}. I should have known that.

cold.li: The {ITEM} has no bearing on outcomes. I stopped pretending otherwise.

plain.li: Since we lost them, I keep watching the clouds. A storm feels like it's coming for someone.
Thunder, then a death. Every time. I've started counting.

gloomy.li: Every time there's a storm, I wait to hear who died.

warm.li: When the thunder starts, I want everyone inside where I can see them. I know it's foolish.

blunt.li: Storm's coming. Stay in. Don't argue.

cheerful.li: I laugh about storms in the daytime. Then the thunder starts, and I go very quiet.

plain.li: I've stopped watching the clouds. A storm is a storm.
I think I could sleep through thunder now.

warm.li: Next time it storms, I'd like to be the one keeping a frightened friend company, not the frightened one.

blunt.li: Done watching the sky. Storms don't pick who dies.

cheerful.li: Lightning is beautiful again. I'd forgotten it could be.

gloomy.li: Storms are only storms again. I'm not sure that's better.

plain.li: I've started praying at night. I don't know to whom. It helps anyway.
Somebody out there must be listening. I've started talking to them every night.

cold.li: I've adopted a nightly ritual. Its efficacy is irrelevant. Its regularity is the point.

warm.li: I pray each night for everyone here, by name. It takes a while now. I don't mind.

blunt.li: I pray at night. Don't interrupt.

cheerful.li: I've started saying a prayer every night, mostly thank-yous.

gloomy.li: I pray every night now. I don't expect an answer. I'd just like someone to know.

plain.li: I lay there unable to move while it went dark around me. Now every dark room feels like that.
[child] I don't like the dark anymore. I want a light by my bed. Please.

warm.li: If anyone else is scared of the dark, they can tell me. I won't laugh.

blunt.li: Leave the lamp burning. I mean it.

cheerful.li: I'm afraid of the dark now, like a child! I'm trying to find that funny.

gloomy.li: The dark feels like lying there again, unable to move. I keep out of it if I can.

plain.li: Walked through a dark room without thinking about it. Only noticed afterward.

warm.li: The dark doesn't bother me now. The others were patient with me while it did, and I won't forget that.

blunt.li: Don't need a light to sleep now.

cheerful.li: I can look up at the night sky again instead of over my shoulder!

gloomy.li: The dark doesn't frighten me anymore. Other things do, but not the dark.

plain.li: Before the fight I touched the doorframe three times and we won. Now I do it every time.
I've got a routine before a fight now. Check, check, the name of someone I've lost, go.

blunt.li: Don't talk to me before a fight. I'm busy.

warm.li: Before each fight I say the names of the people behind me. Then I go.

cheerful.li: Two taps, one deep breath and a bad joke before every fight. It works, so I'm keeping it.

gloomy.li: I do the same things before every fight, in the same order. If I change one, I'm sure that'll be the time.

cold.li: A fixed routine before combat steadies the hands. I don't care whether it's superstition.

plain.li: If my dream could come true, so can the other ones. The one with the black sun.

warm.li: When the sun goes dark, I'll be the one bringing everyone inside. I've decided that much.

blunt.li: If the sun goes out, I'm going in.

gloomy.li: My dream came true. Now I keep looking at the sun and waiting for it to go out.

cold.li: Dreams don't predict anything. I still look up at the sun more often than I'd like.

plain.li: Next time it rains, I'm going out to stand in it until I'm soaked through. I think it'll help.

cheerful.li: Rain is free and it falls on everyone! I'm going to go stand in it every time.

warm.li: I want to stand out in the rain and let it wash the worst of this off me.

blunt.li: I stand in the rain now. It helps. Leave me be.

gloomy.li: The rain doesn't wash anything away. It feels like it does, for a while.

plain.li: The rain can fall without me in it now. I'll watch from inside like everyone else.

warm.li: Rain's for watching from the doorway now, with a friend beside me.

blunt.li: Rain's just rain again. Staying dry.

cheerful.li: Next time it rains I'll stay in and stay dry, and that feels like a good sign.

gloomy.li: The rain's stopped helping. Whatever it was washing away, it's gone or it's stuck.

plain.li: When I was lying there I kept looking at the sky. I'd never really looked before. I mean to look every day now.

warm.li: Food tastes better under the sky. I'd eat every meal out there if I could.

blunt.li: Need the sky. Indoors too long and I start pacing.

cheerful.li: The sky is the best roof there is. Any break I get, I want to spend under it.

gloomy.li: Lying there, all I could see was the sky. Now walls feel like a lid.

cold.li: I think more clearly without a ceiling. I'd work outside if I could.

plain.li: A day under a roof doesn't wear on me like it did.

warm.li: I used to need the sky every day. Now I just like it.

cheerful.li: The sky and I are on easy terms now. I'll see it when I see it.

gloomy.li: The walls don't press in like they did. I suppose I've got used to them.

plain.li: Winter's going to be their season now. I can feel it already.

warm.li: When winter comes I'll keep a light burning for them every night until the thaw.

blunt.li: Winter's for remembering them. That's how it is now.

gloomy.li: Every snowfall from now on will be about them. I don't think that'll change.

cold.li: I expect to be worse in winter now, after the loss. I'll plan around it.

plain.li: I thought of them when the cold came, and then I got on with the day. It's easier now.

warm.li: I can remember them in winter with a smile now, not tears. They'd like that.

cheerful.li: I can laugh in winter again without feeling guilty about it!

gloomy.li: Winter's still hard, but it's not their winter anymore. It's just winter.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: knocks on wood
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: glad after a fight they came through unhurt

plain.li: When someone says things are going well, I knock on wood. You can laugh. We're still alive.

warm.li: I knock on wood when anyone says something hopeful. I want their hopes to last.

blunt.li: Don't say it's quiet. I'll have to knock on something.

cheerful.li: Things are going great! Hang on, let me find some wood.

gloomy.li: Every good thing that's ever been said here was followed by a raid. So I knock.

cold.li: Knocking on wood costs nothing. I do it in case I'm wrong about it.

plain.li: I've started telling the ones we lost about my day. Someone should keep them up to date.

warm.li: I talk to the ones we lost. I tell them we're all right, which is mostly true.

blunt.li: The dead are easy to talk to. They don't interrupt.

cheerful.li: I tell the dead all the good news. It seems only fair they hear it.

gloomy.li: Some days talking to the dead feels like the only conversation I'm any good at.

cold.li: I talk to the dead. It organizes my thoughts.

ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.label: counts everything
ColonyCouncil.QuirkDef.effect: goes over the food stores in their free time, and tells you when the food won't last the week

plain.li: Seven steps from my bed to the door. Twelve to the table. I don't know why I count now. It helps.

warm.li: I count the people at supper every night. Everyone's there. I count again anyway.

blunt.li: Forty-one steps to the stockpile. I counted. Don't ask.

cheerful.li: Counted every bowl we own today, twice! It's oddly soothing.

gloomy.li: I count everything now. Bowls, steps, heads. As if counting kept it all from going missing.

cold.li: I keep counts of things now. Numbers don't lie to me.

plain.li: My grandmother salted the doorstep to keep bad things out. I've started doing the same.

warm.li: I salt the doors of the ones I care about too. They don't have to believe in it.

blunt.li: Salt on the step. Don't sweep it.

cheerful.li: A line of salt across the doorway every night, and nothing bad has got in yet.

gloomy.li: I salt the doorway each night. I know it won't help. I can't stop.
